To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 2000s aspen mortality event was unprecedented in the historical climate record, was associated with high growing season temperatures and low shallow soil water reserves, and was most strongly associated with the spatial pattern of aspen mortality in Colorado.

1) Aspen mortality was triggered by a severe drought that depleted shallow soil moisture, and 2) Aspen mortality occurred in areas that experienced the highest 2002 summer temperatures and the lowest shallow soil moisture.

(i) aspens in Colorado rely on shallow soil moisture during drought stress, (ii) the drought responsible for widespread aspen mortality was characterized by high summer temperature and low soil moisture, and (iii) high summer temperature and shallow soil moisture were the most important climate characteristics associated with the spatial pattern of aspen mortality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of climate change in triggering the recent widespread mortality event in aspen stands across Colorado and the Rocky Mountains.
the role of drought characteristics on aspen forest mortality.
the role of climate change in the widespread aspen forest die‐off across Colorado, USA, and provides insight into how climate characteristics influence forest mortality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2000s drought was the most extreme drought of the past 100 years, with a high temperature and high evaporative demand.
aspen mortality was caused by the 2002 growing‐season drought.
drought is the primary cause of widespread trembling aspen (populus tremuloidis) mortality in Colorado, but the specific drought characteristics that trigger mortality are not well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aspen trees are very vulnerable to drought and that this vulnerability is increasing.
the 2000–2002 drought was the worst drought in Colorado in 100 years and it killed a large number of aspen trees.
drought is an important factor in aspen mortality, and the severity, duration, and timing of the drought can be critical.
The main takeaway from our work is that

aspen mortality is a function of both the timing of drought and the severity of drought, with the timing of the drought being more important in the short term and the severity of the drought being important in the long term.
drought seasonality, duration, and intensity are important factors in determining the vulnerability of forests to mortality.

drought characteristics, such as the timing, duration, severity, and seasonality, are critical for understanding and predicting forest mortality and should be considered in future climate change scenarios and vulnerability assessments.
